name: Vitamin B12
description: Water-soluble vitamin essential for red blood cell formation, neurological function and DNA synthesis.

risks.label: Deficiency risk (vegans/elderly)
risks.context: NIH sets RDA at 2.4 mcg/day. Vegans and adults over 50 absorb less B12 via intrinsic factor and may need supplements.

benefits.label: Red blood cell formation
benefits.context: Prevents megaloblastic anemia by supporting normal RBC maturation.

benefits.label: Neurological health
benefits.context: Maintains the myelin sheath protecting nerve fibres from damage.

benefits.label: Energy metabolism
benefits.context: Cofactor for methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Fatigue, neuropathy, memory loss, depression, pernicious anemia.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: No known toxicity; excess excreted in urine.

importantNotes: Vegans and older adults are at high deficiency risk and may need supplements.
Absorption requires intrinsic factor produced in the stomach.

name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA)
description: Long-chain polyunsaturated fats critical for brain, heart and anti-inflammatory function.

risks.label: Bleeding risk at very high doses
risks.context: FDA considers up to 3 g/day generally safe. >5 g/day may impair platelet aggregation.

benefits.label: Heart health
benefits.context: Lowers triglycerides 15-30%, modestly reduces blood pressure.

benefits.label: Brain function
benefits.context: DHA is the dominant structural fat in neuronal membranes.

benefits.label: Anti-inflammatory
benefits.context: Generates resolvins and protectins that reduce chronic inflammation.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Dry skin, hair loss, immune dysfunction, mood disorders.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Bleeding tendency, fishy aftertaste, GI upset at very high doses.

importantNotes: Plant ALA from flax/chia converts poorly (<10%) to EPA/DHA.
Pregnant women should avoid high-mercury fish.

name: Vitamin A (Retinol)
description: Fat-soluble vitamin essential for vision, immune function, reproduction and cell signalling.

risks.label: Hypervitaminosis A (preformed retinol)
risks.context: Chronic intake above 3000 mcg/day raises liver toxicity, bone fragility and birth-defect risk.

benefits.label: Eye health
benefits.context: Retinal converts to 11-cis-retinal — pigment for low-light vision.

benefits.label: Immune function
benefits.context: Maintains epithelial integrity and white-cell differentiation.

benefits.label: Skin & growth
benefits.context: Drives keratinocyte turnover and embryonic growth signalling.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Night blindness, xerophthalmia, immune impairment, growth retardation.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Headache, nausea, hepatotoxicity, teratogenicity in pregnancy.

importantNotes: Pregnant women must avoid high-dose retinol.
β-carotene precursor has no UL.

name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
description: Water-soluble B-vitamin acting as coenzyme for carbohydrate metabolism and nerve function.

risks.label: Deficiency in alcoholism
risks.context: Alcohol blocks thiamine absorption; chronic deficiency causes beriberi and Wernicke-Korsakoff.

benefits.label: Energy metabolism
benefits.context: Cofactor for pyruvate and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenases.

benefits.label: Nervous system
benefits.context: Required for synthesis of acetylcholine and GABA.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: No known toxicity from food or oral supplements.

importantNotes: Heat- and water-sensitive; lost in milling.
Heavy alcohol depletes body thiamine.

name: Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)
description: Precursor of FAD/FMN coenzymes used in redox reactions and energy production.

risks.label: Deficiency (ariboflavinosis)
risks.context: Rare in developed countries. Pregnancy and athletic training raise needs.

benefits.label: Energy production
benefits.context: FAD and FMN power the electron-transport chain.

benefits.label: Antioxidant recycling
benefits.context: Regenerates glutathione via glutathione reductase.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Excess excreted in urine; bright yellow urine; no toxicity.

importantNotes: Light-sensitive; lost from milk in clear bottles.
High-dose used clinically for migraine prophylaxis.

name: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
description: Precursor of NAD/NADP coenzymes used in over 400 enzymatic reactions.

risks.label: Niacin flush & hepatotoxicity
risks.context: Doses above 35 mg cause flushing; gram-level pharmaceutical doses can cause hepatotoxicity.

benefits.label: Energy metabolism
benefits.context: NAD+/NADP+ drive glycolysis, β-oxidation and the citric-acid cycle.

benefits.label: Lipid profile
benefits.context: Pharmacologic doses raise HDL and lower LDL/triglycerides.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Flushing, liver injury at gram-level pharmacologic doses.

importantNotes: ~60 mg tryptophan converts to 1 mg niacin.
Time-release pharmaceutical niacin requires medical supervision.

name: Vitamin B5 (Pantothenic Acid)
description: Component of coenzyme A and acyl-carrier protein, central to fatty-acid metabolism.

risks.label: Deficiency (very rare)
risks.context: Found widely in foods so deficiency is uncommon.

benefits.label: Energy metabolism
benefits.context: Forms CoA, central to acetyl-CoA and the citric-acid cycle.

benefits.label: Hormone synthesis
benefits.context: Required for adrenal steroid production.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Burning feet, fatigue, irritability, GI upset.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: No known toxicity; very high doses may cause diarrhea.

importantNotes: Name from Greek 'pantothen' meaning 'from everywhere'.
Used topically (panthenol) in skincare.

name: Biotin (Vitamin B7)
description: B-vitamin coenzyme for carboxylase enzymes; popularly marketed for hair, skin and nails.

risks.label: Lab assay interference
risks.context: Doses ≥5000 mcg can falsify thyroid, troponin and hormone immunoassays — FDA 2017 alert.

benefits.label: Macronutrient metabolism
benefits.context: Cofactor of acetyl-CoA, propionyl-CoA and pyruvate carboxylases.

benefits.label: Hair, skin & nails
benefits.context: Evidence supports use for confirmed deficiency; cosmetic claims weakly supported.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Hair loss, brittle nails, scaly skin, depression — rare.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: No known toxicity; lab-test interference at megadoses.

importantNotes: Avidin in raw egg whites blocks biotin absorption.
Stop biotin 48 h before blood tests.

name: Chloride
description: Major extracellular anion regulating fluid balance, gastric acid and acid-base status.

risks.label: Excess intake (with sodium)
risks.context: Mostly from salt; high chloride mirrors high sodium and contributes to hypertension.

benefits.label: Fluid balance
benefits.context: Counter-ion to sodium maintains plasma osmolarity.

benefits.label: Stomach acid
benefits.context: Component of HCl in gastric juice for digestion.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Rare; hypochloremic alkalosis from prolonged vomiting/diuretics.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Tracks with high-sodium diet — hypertension risk.

importantNotes: 1 g salt contains ~600 mg chloride.
Limit processed foods to lower intake.

name: Lutein and Zeaxanthin
description: Yellow xanthophyll carotenoids that concentrate in the macula and protect retinal cells from oxidation.

risks.label: Carotenodermia at megadose
risks.context: Harmless yellowing of skin can occur above 20 mg/day for months.

benefits.label: Macular protection
benefits.context: AREDS2 showed 10 mg lutein + 2 mg zeaxanthin reduces AMD progression by ~25%.

benefits.label: Blue-light filtering
benefits.context: Macular pigment absorbs 400-500 nm light, reducing photo-oxidative stress.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Macular pigment thinning, increased AMD risk.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Yellowing of skin (carotenodermia).

importantNotes: Fat-soluble — eat with healthy fats.
AREDS2 formula recommended for at-risk adults.

name: Curcumin (Turmeric)
description: Yellow polyphenol from Curcuma longa with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects.

risks.label: GI upset / bleeding interaction
risks.context: JECFA ADI 0-3 mg/kg bw/day. Very high doses may potentiate anticoagulants.

benefits.label: Anti-inflammatory
benefits.context: Inhibits NF-κB and COX-2; modestly improves osteoarthritis pain.

benefits.label: Antioxidant defence
benefits.context: Scavenges ROS and induces Nrf2 antioxidant pathway.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Nausea, diarrhea, possible interaction with blood thinners.

importantNotes: Bioavailability boosted ~2000% by piperine.
Avoid in active gallstone disease.

name: Carnitine
description: Quaternary amine that transports long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for β-oxidation.

risks.label: TMAO production
risks.context: Gut microbes convert L-carnitine to TMAO, linked to atherosclerosis in observational studies.

benefits.label: Fatty-acid β-oxidation
benefits.context: Without carnitine, long-chain fats cannot enter mitochondria for energy.

benefits.label: Cardiac support
benefits.context: May modestly improve exercise capacity in heart-failure and angina patients.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Genetic primary deficiency causes cardiomyopathy in infants.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Fishy body odor, GI upset, possible TMAO-related cardiac risk.

importantNotes: L-carnitine is the active form.
Vegans have lower stores but rarely deficient.

name: Glucosamine
description: Amino sugar synthesised endogenously and used as supplement for joint health.

risks.label: Mild GI upset / shellfish allergy
risks.context: Most glucosamine is sourced from shellfish; most preparations are well tolerated up to 1500 mg/day.

benefits.label: Osteoarthritis symptom relief
benefits.context: Modest knee-pain relief in some trials; effects vary by sulphate vs hydrochloride form.

benefits.label: Cartilage matrix support
benefits.context: Substrate for glycosaminoglycan synthesis in cartilage.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: GI upset, headache, drowsiness.

importantNotes: Sulphate form has better trial evidence than hydrochloride.
Caution in shellfish allergy.

name: Chondroitin Sulfate
description: Sulphated glycosaminoglycan that retains water in cartilage matrix.

risks.label: Anticoagulant interaction
risks.context: Structurally similar to heparin; theoretical bleeding risk with warfarin.

benefits.label: Osteoarthritis pain
benefits.context: GAIT trial showed modest pain relief in moderate-severe knee OA.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Mild GI upset.

importantNotes: Often combined with glucosamine.
Quality varies — choose USP-verified products.

name: MSM (Methylsulfonylmethane)
description: Organic sulphur compound used for joint and connective-tissue support.

risks.label: GI symptoms
risks.context: Generally well tolerated up to 4 g/day; higher doses cause nausea, diarrhea.

benefits.label: Joint pain & inflammation
benefits.context: Small trials show reduced osteoarthritis pain; mechanism via sulphur donation and antioxidant pathways.

sources: Trace amounts in fruits, vegetables, milk

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Nausea, diarrhea, headache at high doses.

importantNotes: Often combined with glucosamine + chondroitin.
Choose distilled, high-purity MSM.

name: Probiotics (Lactobacillus acidophilus)
description: Live beneficial bacteria that support gut microbiome diversity and digestive health.

risks.label: Bacteremia in immunocompromised
risks.context: Rare but serious — avoid in central-line patients, severe immunosuppression, premature infants.

benefits.label: Digestive health
benefits.context: Reduces antibiotic-associated diarrhea by ~50% in meta-analyses.

benefits.label: Immune modulation
benefits.context: Modulates gut-associated lymphoid tissue and short-chain fatty-acid production.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Mild bloating; rare bacteremia.

importantNotes: Strain-specific effects; check labels for clinically studied strains.
Refrigerate live products.

name: Prebiotics (FOS/FOS)
description: Fructo-oligosaccharides — non-digestible carbohydrates that selectively feed beneficial gut bacteria.

risks.label: Bloating / gas
risks.context: Doses above 10 g/day commonly cause flatulence and abdominal discomfort.

benefits.label: Bifidobacteria growth
benefits.context: Selectively increase Bifidobacteria producing short-chain fatty acids.

benefits.label: Calcium absorption
benefits.context: Inulin/FOS modestly enhance calcium and magnesium absorption.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Bloating, gas, abdominal cramping.

importantNotes: Increase intake gradually.
Avoid in IBS during low-FODMAP phase.

benefits.context: Activates ATP, regulates NMDA receptors and supports muscle relaxation.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Diarrhea, hypotension, cardiac issues at megadose.

importantNotes: Glycinate and citrate forms absorb better.
Common deficiency in Western diets.

name: Zinc
description: Essential trace mineral cofactor for >100 enzymes.

risks.label: Copper deficiency at high zinc
risks.context: Chronic >40 mg/day suppresses copper absorption causing anaemia and neuropathy.

benefits.label: Immune function
benefits.context: Supports T-cell maturation; lozenges may shorten cold duration.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Impaired immunity, hair loss, growth retardation, hypogonadism.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Nausea, copper deficiency, immune suppression at chronic high doses.

importantNotes: Phytates in grains/legumes reduce absorption.
Picolinate and citrate forms absorb well.

name: Potassium
description: Major intracellular cation regulating blood pressure and nerve impulses.

risks.label: Hyperkalemia in CKD
risks.context: Patients with chronic kidney disease or on ACE-inhibitors must limit potassium to avoid arrhythmia.

benefits.label: Blood pressure control
benefits.context: Counteracts sodium's pressor effect — DASH diet emphasises potassium-rich foods.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Hyperkalaemia — cardiac arrhythmia (mainly in CKD).

importantNotes: WHO recommends ≥3510 mg/day adults.
Caution with K-sparing diuretics.

name: Sodium
description: Major extracellular cation regulating fluid balance and nerve transmission.

risks.label: Hypertension & CV disease
risks.context: WHO recommends <2000 mg/day. Chronic excess raises blood pressure and CVD risk.

benefits.label: Fluid & nerve function
benefits.context: Maintains plasma osmolarity, action potentials and nutrient transport.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Rare in diet — hyponatremia from excess water or endurance events.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Hypertension, stroke, kidney damage.

importantNotes: 1 g salt = 400 mg sodium.
Replace processed with whole foods to lower intake.

name: Phosphorus
description: Mineral component of bone (hydroxyapatite), DNA and ATP.

risks.label: High phosphate in CKD
risks.context: Excess inorganic phosphate (in processed foods) accelerates vascular calcification in kidney disease.

benefits.label: Bone & energy
benefits.context: Forms hydroxyapatite and high-energy ATP bonds.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: High intake from cola/processed foods linked to bone loss in CKD.

importantNotes: Inorganic phosphate (additives) absorbs ~100% vs organic ~60%.
Watch phosphate additives in processed meat.

name: Iodine
description: Essential component of thyroid hormones T3 and T4.

risks.label: Hyperthyroidism / goitre
risks.context: Excess iodine can paradoxically cause goitre, Hashimoto's flares and iodine-induced hyperthyroidism.

benefits.label: Thyroid function
benefits.context: Substrate for thyroid hormone synthesis controlling metabolism, growth and brain development.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Goitre, cretinism, intellectual disability in offspring.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Thyroiditis, hyperthyroidism.

importantNotes: Universal salt iodisation eliminates deficiency.
Pregnancy needs +70 mcg/day.

name: Copper
description: Trace mineral cofactor for cytochrome-c oxidase and superoxide dismutase.

risks.label: Wilson's disease overload
risks.context: Genetic Wilson's disease causes copper accumulation; chronic excess from supplements can cause hepatitis.

benefits.label: Energy & connective tissue
benefits.context: Cofactor for ETC and lysyl oxidase (cross-linking collagen and elastin).

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Liver damage, GI upset.

importantNotes: High zinc intake antagonises copper.
Wilson's disease requires lifelong copper restriction.

name: Manganese
description: Trace mineral cofactor for SOD2 and bone formation enzymes.

risks.label: Neurotoxicity from inhalation
risks.context: Chronic inhalation (welders) causes manganism. Dietary excess rare; extremely high water content can affect cognition.

benefits.label: Antioxidant defence
benefits.context: Cofactor for mitochondrial SOD2 and bone glycosyltransferases.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Neurological symptoms; rare from food.

importantNotes: Highest in tea (theanine source).
Caution with manganese-rich water.

name: Chromium
description: Trace mineral that may potentiate insulin signalling.

risks.label: Hexavalent toxicity
risks.context: Trivalent dietary Cr is safe up to 1000 mcg/day; hexavalent (industrial) is carcinogenic.

benefits.label: Glucose metabolism
benefits.context: Modest fasting-glucose improvement at 200-1000 mcg in some trials.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Rare from food; supplements >1000 mcg/day may cause GI upset.

importantNotes: Chromium picolinate is the most studied form.
Type-2 diabetes evidence is mixed.

name: Molybdenum
description: Trace mineral cofactor for sulfite oxidase and xanthine oxidase.

risks.label: Gout flare-up
risks.context: Doses >2000 mcg/day raise uric acid and may trigger gout.

benefits.label: Sulphite detoxification
benefits.context: Sulfite oxidase converts sulfite to sulfate, preventing neurological damage.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Gout, hyperuricemia, copper imbalance.

importantNotes: Plant intake is generally adequate.
Soil content varies regionally.

name: Fluoride
description: Trace mineral that hardens enamel and inhibits caries.

risks.label: Dental & skeletal fluorosis
risks.context: Chronic intake >10 mg/day causes mottled teeth and bone fragility.

benefits.label: Caries prevention
benefits.context: Forms fluorapatite that resists acid demineralisation.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Fluorosis, bone fragility.

importantNotes: Optimal water fluoridation 0.7 mg/L.
Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste.

name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids
description: Family of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids — ALA, EPA, DHA.

risks.label: Bleeding at very high dose
risks.context: >5 g/day may impair platelet function.

benefits.label: Cardiovascular protection
benefits.context: Lowers triglycerides, blood pressure and arterial inflammation.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Mood disorders, dry skin, poor cognition.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Bleeding tendency at megadoses.

importantNotes: WHO recommends 1-2 servings oily fish/week.
Plant ALA → EPA conversion is <10%.

name: Omega-6 Fatty Acids
description: Polyunsaturated linoleic acid (LA) and arachidonic acid (AA).

risks.label: Pro-inflammatory at high omega-6:3 ratio
risks.context: Modern diets reach 20:1 omega-6:3 ratios; ideal is 4:1 or lower.

benefits.label: Skin barrier & growth
benefits.context: Linoleic acid is essential for ceramide synthesis and growth.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Skin changes, growth retardation in infants.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: May exacerbate inflammation when omega-3 intake is low.

importantNotes: Improve omega-6:3 ratio via fish & flax intake.
EFSA AI: 4% energy.

name: Dietary Fiber
description: Non-digestible plant carbohydrates supporting colonic health and metabolic regulation.

risks.label: Bloating / mineral binding
risks.context: Rapid increases cause gas; phytate fibre binds minerals.

benefits.label: Cholesterol & glucose control
benefits.context: Soluble fibre (β-glucan, pectin) lowers LDL by 5-10% and slows glucose absorption.

benefits.label: Microbiome SCFA
benefits.context: Fermented to butyrate fueling colonocytes and reducing colorectal cancer risk.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Gas, bloating, mineral malabsorption.

importantNotes: Increase intake gradually with adequate water.
WHO ≥25 g/day adults.

name: Protein
description: Macronutrient providing amino acids for tissue repair, enzymes and hormones.

risks.label: Kidney load in CKD
risks.context: High intake increases hyperfiltration; healthy kidneys tolerate well, CKD requires restriction.

benefits.label: Tissue maintenance
benefits.context: Provides essential amino acids for muscle, enzymes, antibodies and hormones.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible kidney strain in CKD; bone calcium loss debated.

importantNotes: IOM RDA 0.8 g/kg/day; older adults benefit from 1.0-1.2 g/kg.
Distribute protein across meals for optimal MPS.

name: Carbohydrates
description: Sugars, starches and fibre — primary energy source providing 4 kcal/g.

risks.label: Excess refined carbs & added sugars
risks.context: WHO: free sugars <10% (ideally <5%) of energy. Excess raises type-2 diabetes and dental caries risk.

benefits.label: Brain & exercise fuel
benefits.context: Brain uses 120 g glucose/day; muscle glycogen powers high-intensity exercise.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Ketosis from very-low-carb diets is generally well tolerated.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Weight gain, dental caries, dyslipidemia from refined carbs.

importantNotes: Choose complex carbs over refined.
WHO: <10% energy from free sugars.

name: Fat
description: Macronutrient supplying 9 kcal/g and essential fatty acids.

risks.label: Saturated & trans fat
risks.context: WHO: limit saturated fat <10% energy and trans fat <1%; excess raises CVD risk.

benefits.label: Vitamin absorption
benefits.context: Required for absorbing fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K.

risksAndDeficiency.deficiency: Essential fatty acid deficiency — skin issues, growth retardation.
risksAndDeficiency.excess: Weight gain; CVD risk if saturated/trans fat dominant.

importantNotes: WHO: 20-35% energy from fat.
Replace saturated with unsaturated fat for CVD reduction.

name: Glucose
description: Six-carbon monosaccharide — primary blood sugar and cellular energy substrate.

risks.label: Glycaemic spikes
risks.context: Free glucose causes rapid blood-sugar rise; chronic excess drives insulin resistance and dental caries.

benefits.label: Cellular energy
benefits.context: Primary substrate for ATP via glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Hyperglycaemia, weight gain, dental caries, type-2 diabetes.

importantNotes: WHO: free sugars <10% of energy.
Athletes use during prolonged exercise.

name: Fructose
description: Six-carbon ketonic monosaccharide naturally present in fruit and high-fructose corn syrup.

risks.label: NAFLD & uric acid
risks.context: Excess fructose (especially HFCS) drives hepatic lipogenesis, uric acid and metabolic syndrome.

benefits.label: Low glycaemic index
benefits.context: Causes smaller blood-glucose rise than sucrose at equivalent energy.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Hepatic steatosis, hyperuricaemia, metabolic syndrome.

importantNotes: Fruit is a healthy source — fibre slows absorption.
Limit added fructose / HFCS.

name: Sucrose
description: Disaccharide of glucose + fructose — common table sugar.

risks.label: Free-sugar overconsumption
risks.context: WHO recommends <10% (ideally <5%) of energy from free sugars; excess raises caries, obesity, T2DM risk.

benefits.label: Quick energy
benefits.context: Splits into glucose + fructose for rapid energy uptake.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Dental caries, weight gain, insulin resistance.

importantNotes: WHO: free sugars <25 g/day for adults.
Hidden in sauces, drinks, breads.

name: Lactose
description: Disaccharide of glucose + galactose found exclusively in milk.

risks.label: Lactose intolerance
risks.context: Adults lacking lactase (≈70% globally) develop bloating and diarrhea above 12 g/day.

benefits.label: Calcium absorption support
benefits.context: Lactose modestly enhances calcium absorption in infants.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Bloating, diarrhea, flatulence in lactose intolerant.

importantNotes: Lactase enzyme (Lactaid) supplements aid digestion.
Hard cheese and yogurt have less lactose.

name: Maltose
description: Disaccharide of two glucose units produced from starch hydrolysis.

risks.label: High glycaemic index
risks.context: Maltose has a GI ≈105, similar to pure glucose; raises blood sugar quickly.

benefits.label: Quick energy
benefits.context: Hydrolyses to glucose for rapid uptake — used in sports drinks.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Same metabolic concerns as added sugars.

importantNotes: Counts as free sugar in WHO guidelines.
GI similar to pure glucose.

name: Starch
description: Polysaccharide of glucose units — main storage carbohydrate in plants.

risks.label: Refined starch & glycaemic load
risks.context: Refined starches (white bread, white rice) drive blood-sugar spikes; whole-grain starch is healthier.

benefits.label: Sustained energy
benefits.context: Slow glucose release supports endurance.

benefits.label: Resistant starch / SCFA
benefits.context: Cooled cooked starches resist digestion and feed colonic bacteria, producing butyrate.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Refined starch overconsumption tied to obesity and diabetes.

importantNotes: Choose intact whole grains.
Cool then reheat starches to boost resistant starch.

name: Beta-Glucan
description: Soluble fibre from oats, barley and mushrooms — recognised by EFSA for cholesterol reduction.

risks.label: Bloating
risks.context: Rapid increases may cause gas; well tolerated otherwise.

benefits.label: LDL cholesterol reduction
benefits.context: EFSA-approved health claim: 3 g β-glucan/day reduces blood cholesterol.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Gas, bloating.

importantNotes: 3 g daily covers EFSA cholesterol claim.
Combines well with low-saturated-fat diet.

name: Pectin
description: Soluble plant fibre and gelling additive (E440) extracted from citrus and apples.

risks.label: GI fullness
risks.context: Generally well tolerated; ADI not specified by JECFA.

benefits.label: Cholesterol & glycaemic control
benefits.context: Forms viscous gel that slows nutrient absorption and lowers LDL.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Bloating, gas.

importantNotes: Approved as E440 thickener.
Combines with sugar to form jam.

name: Inulin
description: Long-chain fructan prebiotic that selectively feeds Bifidobacteria.

risks.label: FODMAP-related bloating
risks.context: High FODMAP — IBS patients may need to limit during low-FODMAP elimination.

benefits.label: Bifidobacteria support
benefits.context: EFSA-approved health claim for normal bowel function at 12 g/day.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Bloating, gas.

importantNotes: Increase intake gradually.
Often used as low-calorie sweetener.

name: Probiotics
description: Generic listing for live beneficial bacteria from fermented foods or supplements.

risks.label: Bacteremia in immunocompromised
risks.context: Avoid in central-line patients, severe immunosuppression and premature infants.

benefits.label: Microbiome modulation
benefits.context: Strain-specific benefits including reduced antibiotic-associated diarrhea and IBS symptom control.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Mild bloating; rare bacteremia.

importantNotes: Choose strains with clinical evidence.
Refrigerate live products.

name: Lycopene
description: Red carotenoid from tomatoes with strong singlet-oxygen quenching activity.

risks.label: Carotenodermia at megadose
risks.context: Doses above 75 mg/day can yellow skin (lycopenoderma), harmless and reversible.

benefits.label: Prostate & cardiovascular protection
benefits.context: Meta-analyses link lycopene to lower prostate-cancer and CVD risk via antioxidant action.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Bioavailability higher in cooked, oil-cooked tomatoes.
Fat-soluble — eat with healthy fats.

name: Beta-Carotene
description: Orange carotenoid that the body converts to vitamin A as needed.

risks.label: Smoker lung-cancer risk
risks.context: ATBC and CARET trials linked high-dose β-carotene supplements (>20 mg/day) with increased lung-cancer risk in smokers.

benefits.label: Vitamin A precursor
benefits.context: 12 mcg β-carotene = 1 mcg RAE retinol; safer than preformed retinol with no toxicity ceiling from food.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Smokers should avoid high-dose β-carotene supplements.
Body regulates conversion to vitamin A.

name: Lutein
description: Yellow xanthophyll concentrated in the macula and lens.

risks.label: Carotenodermia
risks.context: Harmless yellowing of skin at chronic high intake.

benefits.label: Macular pigment density
benefits.context: Increases macular pigment optical density, slowing AMD progression.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: AREDS2 dose: 10 mg.
Best paired with zeaxanthin.

name: Zeaxanthin
description: Yellow xanthophyll partner of lutein in macular pigment.

risks.label: Carotenodermia at megadose
risks.context: Excess can yellow skin reversibly.

benefits.label: Central macular protection
benefits.context: Concentrates in central fovea, filters blue light and reduces oxidative damage.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: AREDS2 dose: 2 mg.
Best taken with fat for absorption.

name: Quercetin
description: Plant flavonol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antihistamine activity.

risks.label: Drug interactions
risks.context: Inhibits CYP3A4 and OATP transporters; may raise levels of cyclosporin, statins and digoxin.

benefits.label: Antihistamine & antioxidant
benefits.context: Stabilises mast cells and scavenges peroxyl radicals; modest BP and exercise-recovery benefits.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Combine with bromelain or vitamin C for absorption.
Generally safe ≤1 g/day for short courses.

name: Resveratrol
description: Stilbenoid polyphenol from grape skins that activates sirtuin pathways in animal models.

risks.label: Drug interactions
risks.context: Inhibits CYP3A4; may potentiate anticoagulants and some statins. EFSA: doses up to 150 mg/day from supplements considered safe.

benefits.label: Cardiovascular & cellular ageing
benefits.context: Activates SIRT1; modest improvements in endothelial function and insulin sensitivity in trials.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Bioavailability low (5%); look for trans-resveratrol.
Avoid in pregnancy.

name: Curcumin
description: Yellow polyphenol from turmeric (alias of primary entry).

risks.label: GI upset / bleeding interaction
risks.context: JECFA ADI 0-3 mg/kg bw/day; very high doses may potentiate anticoagulants.

benefits.label: Anti-inflammatory & antioxidant
benefits.context: Inhibits NF-κB and COX-2; modest osteoarthritis pain relief in trials.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Piperine boosts bioavailability ~2000%.
Avoid in active gallstone disease.

name: Epigallocatechin Gallate (EGCG)
description: Major catechin in green tea with antioxidant and metabolic effects.

risks.label: Hepatotoxicity at megadose
risks.context: EFSA flags doses >800 mg/day from supplements as risk of liver injury.

benefits.label: Cardio-metabolic support
benefits.context: Modest reductions in LDL and body fat in meta-analyses.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: EFSA: limit isolated EGCG supplements to <800 mg/day.
Brewed tea is safer than concentrates.

name: Anthocyanins
description: Water-soluble pigments giving red/blue/purple colour and acting as antioxidants.

risks.label: Stains teeth / oxalate
risks.context: Generally safe; berry oxalate may raise stone risk in susceptible individuals.

benefits.label: Vascular & cognitive benefits
benefits.context: Improve endothelial function and may slow age-related cognitive decline.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Best from whole berries.
Cooking destroys some anthocyanins.

name: Polyphenols
description: Broad family of plant secondary metabolites including flavonoids, lignans and phenolic acids.

risks.label: Iron absorption inhibition
risks.context: Tannins and phytate-bound polyphenols can reduce non-heme iron uptake when consumed with meals.

benefits.label: Cardiometabolic protection
benefits.context: Mediterranean-diet polyphenol intake associated with lower CVD and all-cause mortality.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Diversity matters more than total grams.
Drink tea/coffee between meals to protect iron uptake.

name: Caffeine
description: Methylxanthine alkaloid that blocks adenosine receptors, raising alertness.

risks.label: Cardiovascular & sleep effects
risks.context: EFSA: ≤400 mg/day adults safe; >600 mg can cause anxiety, insomnia, arrhythmia. Pregnancy ≤200 mg.

benefits.label: Cognitive performance
benefits.context: Improves alertness and reaction time at 1-3 mg/kg.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Pregnancy: limit to 200 mg/day (~2 cups coffee).
Avoid pure powdered caffeine — fatal at 10 g.

name: Chlorogenic Acid
description: Polyphenol abundant in coffee with modest blood-pressure-lowering effect.

risks.label: Plasma homocysteine
risks.context: High coffee intake can raise homocysteine via chlorogenic acid; offset with adequate folate.

benefits.label: Blood pressure & glucose
benefits.context: Trials show ~3-5 mmHg systolic BP reduction at 400-800 mg/day.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Heavy roasts contain less.
Green-coffee-bean extract is concentrated source.

name: Tannins
description: Group of polyphenols that bind proteins and minerals, giving astringent taste.

risks.label: Mineral absorption interference
risks.context: Inhibit non-heme iron and zinc uptake; consume tea/coffee between meals.

benefits.label: Antimicrobial & antioxidant
benefits.context: Bind microbial proteins and quench radicals; condensed tannins (proanthocyanidins) protect cardiovascular tissue.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Avoid with iron-rich meals.
Cooking and aging often reduce astringency.

name: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10)
description: Lipid-soluble quinone shuttling electrons in the mitochondrial respiratory chain.

risks.label: Anticoagulant interaction
risks.context: Structurally similar to vitamin K — may reduce warfarin efficacy.

benefits.label: Cellular energy
benefits.context: Restores tissue CoQ10 depleted by statins; modest blood-pressure and migraine benefit.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Ubiquinol form better absorbed than ubiquinone.
Take with fat-containing meal.

name: L-Glutamine
description: Most abundant free amino acid; primary fuel for enterocytes (alias for Glutamine entry).

risks.label: Liver / kidney load
risks.context: Caution in cirrhosis and Reye-syndrome history; excess ammonia generation possible.

benefits.label: Gut barrier support
benefits.context: Replenishes enteric stores depleted in catabolic stress; helps post-surgery recovery.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Often used in burns, sepsis, IBD support.
Different free vs peptide-bound forms.

name: Creatine
description: Tripeptide stored in muscle as phosphocreatine for rapid ATP regeneration.

risks.label: Mild water retention
risks.context: 2-4 lb water-weight gain in muscle; safe for healthy kidneys.

benefits.label: Strength & cognition
benefits.context: Boosts max effort, lean mass and may aid working memory in older adults.

sources: Endogenous synthesis from arginine + glycine + methionine

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Monohydrate form is the most studied.
No loading dose needed; 3-5 g/day suffices.

name: Taurine
description: Sulphonic-acid amino acid abundant in heart, brain and bile.

risks.label: Energy-drink stacking
risks.context: EFSA: 6 g/day safe alone but combined with caffeine in energy drinks may stress cardiovascular system.

benefits.label: Cardiac & retinal support
benefits.context: Stabilises cell membranes and Ca²⁺ handling; deficiency causes cardiomyopathy in cats.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Vegans rely on endogenous synthesis.
Often added to energy drinks.

name: L-Carnitine
description: Active L-isomer of carnitine — transports fatty acids into mitochondria (alias).

risks.label: TMAO formation
risks.context: Gut bacteria convert L-carnitine to TMAO, linked to atherosclerosis in observational studies.

benefits.label: Energy & cardiac function
benefits.context: May modestly improve exercise capacity in heart-failure patients.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: L-carnitine only — avoid D-carnitine.
Vegans have lower stores but rarely deficient.

name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
description: Sulphur-containing antioxidant active in both aqueous and lipid phases.

risks.label: Hypoglycaemia / thyroid suppression
risks.context: May lower blood glucose — caution in diabetics; megadose may suppress thyroid hormones.

benefits.label: Diabetic neuropathy
benefits.context: EMA-approved in Germany at 600 mg/day for diabetic peripheral neuropathy symptoms.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: R-form is the natural enantiomer.
Take on empty stomach for best absorption.

name: Glutathione
description: Tripeptide (glu-cys-gly) and major intracellular antioxidant.

risks.label: Poor oral bioavailability
risks.context: Oral GSH is largely degraded; liposomal or IV may bypass digestion. IV use should be medically supervised.

benefits.label: Detoxification
benefits.context: Conjugates xenobiotics for excretion and recycles vitamins C and E.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: NAC supplementation raises endogenous GSH effectively.
Avoid IV outside medical supervision.

name: Melatonin
description: Pineal-gland hormone derived from tryptophan; regulates circadian rhythm.

risks.label: Daytime grogginess / hormonal effects
risks.context: Doses >5 mg may cause morning grogginess and rarely affect reproductive hormones in adolescents.

benefits.label: Sleep onset & jet-lag
benefits.context: 0.5-3 mg taken 30-60 min pre-bed reduces sleep-onset latency and helps jet-lag.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Lower doses (0.3-1 mg) often as effective as higher.
Discuss with paediatrician before giving to children.

name: Collagen
description: Most abundant body protein, structural in skin, bone, cartilage and connective tissue.

risks.label: Source allergens
risks.context: Bovine, marine or porcine origin — allergy possible.

benefits.label: Skin & joint support
benefits.context: Hydrolysed collagen 2.5-10 g/day improves skin hydration and elasticity in trials.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Type I/III for skin; Type II for joints.
Best with vitamin C for synthesis.

name: Hyaluronic Acid
description: Glycosaminoglycan in synovial fluid and skin matrix retaining water.

risks.label: Injection-site reactions
risks.context: Intra-articular and dermal-filler injections require qualified clinicians.

benefits.label: Skin & joint hydration
benefits.context: Oral 120-240 mg/day improved skin moisture in 12-week trials.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Choose low-MW (~50 kDa) for systemic absorption.
Often combined with collagen and vitamin C.

name: Choline
description: Vitamin-like nutrient required for phosphatidylcholine, acetylcholine and methylation.

risks.label: Fishy body odour / TMAO
risks.context: Gut microbes convert excess choline to TMAO — linked to CVD in observational studies.

benefits.label: Brain & liver health
benefits.context: Crucial for fetal brain development and hepatic VLDL export.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Pregnancy needs 450 mg/day for fetal brain.
Limit if you have TMAU.

name: Inositol
description: Cyclitol (myo-inositol) involved in insulin signalling and PCOS management.

risks.label: GI symptoms
risks.context: Doses >12 g/day can cause nausea and diarrhea.

benefits.label: PCOS & insulin sensitivity
benefits.context: Myo + d-chiro inositol (40:1) improves ovulation and insulin sensitivity in PCOS.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Combine myo + d-chiro inositol 40:1.
Pregnancy use mostly safe but discuss with OB.

name: Sulforaphane
description: Isothiocyanate from broccoli sprouts; activates Nrf2 antioxidant pathway.

risks.label: Goitrogenic at megadose
risks.context: Glucosinolate parent may impair iodine uptake; manage iodine intake if consuming high amounts.

benefits.label: Detox & cellular protection
benefits.context: Up-regulates phase-II detox enzymes; may modestly aid blood-pressure and autism trials are ongoing.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Sprouts contain 50-100x sulforaphane vs mature broccoli.
Lightly steam (3 min) to preserve myrosinase enzyme.

name: Allicin
description: Sulphur compound formed when garlic is crushed; antimicrobial and BP-lowering.

risks.label: GI / bleeding interaction
risks.context: Antiplatelet effect — caution before surgery and with anticoagulants.

benefits.label: Cardiovascular & antimicrobial
benefits.context: Aged garlic reduces systolic BP by ~5-9 mmHg in meta-analyses.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Crush and rest 10 min before cooking to maximise allicin.
Aged garlic extract (AGE) is gentler on the stomach.

name: Capsaicin
description: Vanilloid responsible for chilli pepper heat; activates TRPV1 receptors.

risks.label: GI irritation
risks.context: Excess can worsen GERD, IBS or hemorrhoids; topical patches may burn skin.

benefits.label: Metabolic & analgesic
benefits.context: Modest thermogenesis and reduced appetite; topical capsaicin reduces neuropathic pain.

risksAndDeficiency.excess: Possible GI upset at high doses.

importantNotes: Wear gloves when chopping hot peppers.
Topical 0.025-0.075% creams used for chronic pain.

name: Berberine
